# Momentus Technologies Launches MomentusMAX, an AI Platform Built for Venues, and Brings MAX for Sales to General Availability

PR Newswire

15 September 20263 min read

_New platform will house Momentus's growing family of AI products; the latest release automates lead scoring, calendar decisions, and proposal building for venue sales teams._

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Momentus Technologies, the global leader in venue and event management, powering more than 4,000 venues worldwide, today announced the general availability of MAX for Sales, an AI-native CRM supporting revenue orchestration and automation. This release marks the launch of MomentusMAX, the new platform that will house a [growing suite of AI products](https://gomomentus.com/ai), with MAX for Sales as its latest offering.

![Momentus Logo JPG Digital](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/4821f3d85de7ef4569290f32847c5c443af3b48c0d970bf4b78ad0e1161821cd/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fprnewswire.com%2F8090e4ca1e240f0c7baf33d6d6825ee5.jpg)

Momentus Logo JPG Digital

Venue sales teams spend up to 70 percent of their week on administrative work rather than selling; triaging leads by hand, checking calendars across multiple spaces, and building proposals from scratch for every inquiry. The cost of that overhead compounds quickly, with up to 50 percent of RFPs going to the first venue to respond and nearly half of all available venue days go unbooked industry-wide.

[MAX for Sales](https://gomomentus.com/max-for-sales) works alongside a venue's existing sales team inside the Momentus platform to optimize these tasks, built around three core engines:

- Lead Engine – automatically captures, deduplicates, and scores every inbound inquiry, so reps see the highest-value opportunities first instead of the loudest ones.

- Calendar Engine – resolves booking conflicts and recommends the highest-value hold using real revenue data, not gut instinct.

- Revenue Engine – builds complete proposals with upsells and projected margin included, not just the room.


From inquiry to proposal, MAX for Sales does the administrative work so sales teams can focus on making the final decision on every recommendation.

"Generic AI doesn't know your venue, your spaces, or your clients. That gap is exactly why it hasn't delivered real value in day-to-day sales work for events," said Alex Griffis, Chief Product Officer, Momentus Technologies. "We built MAX for Sales as a context layer on top of a venue's own data, so it actually understands their business, not just business in general."

MomentusMAX will expand over the next year with MAX for Events, focused on planning and day-of operational execution, and MAX for Finance, focused on revenue recognition, cost optimization, and forecasting, extending the same purpose-built approach across the full venue lifecycle, from lead to invoice.

"When AI first came out, everyone was very cautious of it, but I view technology as a way to help me do my job, not take my job. It's exciting because Momentus is looking at what event management clients like us need and building tools like MAX for Sales that allow us to do our jobs in a more efficient and better way." said Gary Firlit, Director of Business Analytics, Floreano Convention Center.

Story continues

MAX for Sales is available now to both [Momentus Enterprise](https://gomomentus.com/enterprise-event-management-software) and [Elite](https://gomomentus.com/venue-management-software) customers. More information is available at [gomomentus.com/max-for-sales](https://gomomentus.com/max-for-sales)

**About Momentus Technologies**

Momentus Technologies is a global provider of industry-leading event and [venue management software](https://gomomentus.com/) that empowers organizations to create extraordinary moments. With over 90,000 users in more than 57 countries, Momentus serves the needs of convention and exhibition centers, trade fairs, higher education, corporate venues, stadiums and arenas, arts and culture centers and more. Its powerful, intuitive platform alongside intelligent data-driven solutions and unparalleled expertise provides customers a view of past, present, and future event operations to increase end-to-end visibility, optimize efficiency, and achieve business goals. Over the past three years, Momentus has invested significantly in AI, cloud infrastructure, and ecosystem partnerships, including the launch of Ask Mo, Momentus Analytics, and Smart Imports, to build the intelligent operating platform for the next generation of venue and event management. Founded in 1985, Momentus is headquartered in the United States with employees working across the globe. To learn more, visit [gomomentus.com](https://gomomentus.com/).

# Meta builds humanoid robot with China’s Fourier as home robot push expands: report













Roushni Nair



31 October 20262 min read

































  - [META \\
    +0.08%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/META/ "META")

  - [NVDA \\
    -6.15%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/ "NVDA")


Investing.com -- Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) has developed a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics startup Fourier and is already working on a second version, The Information reported on Saturday, as the Facebook parent steps up efforts to bring AI into everyday household tasks.

The prototype, internally named Max, weighs about 106 pounds and was built by the two companies in roughly three months, according to people familiar with the project cited by The Information.

Standing around 1.5 metres tall, the robot uses Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip and features a display capable of mimicking facial expressions, built-in speakers and five-fingered hands designed to handle small objects, according to the report.

Meta's robotics team travelled to China to work with Fourier, with the company's vice president of product for robotics, Li-Chen Miller, spending almost two months at the startup's Shanghai factory, the report said. Max was demonstrated to some Meta employees at an internal robotics summit in late August.

The companies began developing a second prototype, Max 2, in September. The updated version is expected to feature a redesigned torso, improved hands for handling objects, a projector and additional sensors to help it navigate stairs, according to the report.

Meta sees humanoid robots as a potential physical extension of its Muse AI agent, with the long-term ambition of developing machines capable of assisting with household tasks. The company has also strengthened its robotics capabilities through its May acquisition of Assured Robot Intelligence, a startup developing AI models that help robots understand and adapt to human behaviour.

However, Meta told The Information that its work with Fourier was focused on internal research and experimentation and that it had no plans to sell the units.

# Boost Run stock surges on AI infrastructure deployment













Luke Juricic



26 October 20262 min read

































  - [BRUN \\
    -5.52%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/BRUN/ "BRUN")


Investing.com -- Boost Run Inc (NASDAQ:BRUN) shares rose 6.7% in after-hours trading Monday following the company's announcement of AI infrastructure deployment and the closing of more than $600 million in non-dilutive project financing year to date.

The Northbrook, Illinois-based company delivered the first project phase to a leading AI research and product company under agreements signed in May 2026. The multi-year agreements provide for the deployment of NVIDIA B300 GPUs across the company's data center facilities, along with related network storage and CPU node services.

In September, Boost Run added a new customer and signed a five-year, $525.6 million AI cloud services agreement with a leading provider of enterprise AI models and solutions. Under the agreement, Boost Run will deliver compute capacity powered by NVIDIA GPUs, along with network storage and CPU node services.

The company has established a fully funded runway to accelerate customer deployments through the fourth quarter of 2026 and scale operations into 2027. Several additional projects are in deployment and are nearing hand-off in the coming weeks, according to the company.

Boost Run is expanding its active colocation footprint across multiple new sites with existing data center partners. The company has extended its Minnesota presence and expects total deployed colocation capacity to reach approximately 40 MW by the end of 2026.

The company's project financing is structured to be repaid before contracts end, with customer payments exceeding debt payments each month. Once debt is repaid, the remaining contract term generates higher margins, according to CEO Andrew Karos.

Boost Run operates as an NVIDIA Preferred Cloud Provider and has achieved NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture. The company maintains SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and ISO 27701 certifications.

# Buy these 2 stocks amid AI financing concerns: Analyst













Rachael Rajan



18 October 20262 min read

































  - [CRWV \\
    -2.65%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CRWV/ "CRWV")

  - [TFC \\
    +0.02%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/TFC/ "TFC")

  - [NBIS \\
    -6.94%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/NBIS/ "NBIS")


Investing.com -- The withdrawal of the Firmus IPO has raised some concerns, but Truist analysts believe it is only a matter of time the quality of the digital platforms and IT services space becomes clear. In their recent note, firm analysts identify two cloud providers with backlogs providing meaningful revenue visibility, and they say the softness in their shares is a buying opportunity.

Amid recent AI financing concerns, Truist recommends buying CoreWeave Inc (NASDAQ:CRWV) and Nebius Group NV (NASDAQ:NBIS) shares.

Truist has Buy rating on both names and a price target of $165 on CRWV stock and $355 on NBIS.

Firm analysts say their multiple assumption for CRWV represents a premium to the median of 21x 2027 EV/EBIT among AI cloud providers and leading providers of AI infrastructure.

Meanwhile, NBIS' 4.5x 2028E EV/Sales multiple on their 2028E revenue estimate is above the peer average in the AI cloud and hyperscaler industry. Truist notes that the premium is warranted given the expectation that NBIS will deliver industry-leading growth rates across 2026E-2028E.

The research firm observes that over the next two years, the AI cloud/neocloud cohort could report strong revenue growth rates given the compute shortage. However, the firm believes that cloud providers that demonstrate the necessary execution, financing, and upstack expansion to build sustainable businesses will distinguish themselves in the coming quarters.

"We continue to see CRWV and NBIS as leaders in the space, with their status as the only two companies holding Platinum rankings on SemiAnalysis's ClusterMax 3.0 providing a further proof point of the quality of their platforms," the analysts said.

To illustrate the difference in scale between Firmus, which has an active capacity of 46MW, on one hand, and CRWV and NBIS on the other, the analysts note CRWV has 1.5GW (1,500MW) and NBIS has ~450MW of active capacity. CRWV's addition of 500MW capacity in Q2 is equivalent to ~10x the total capacity each company has brought online in their corporate history.

Truist emphasises that these numbers represent the actual capacity that AI clouds will be able to recognise revenue on. Furthermore, companies with larger backlogs and limited active capacity will face a higher execution hurdle if they must catch up and generate revenue.

Both CRWV and NBIS are receiving more upfront payments and collecting pre-payments on 70% of recent deals, allowing them to get by with less external capital, Truist added.

# MaxCyte stock surges 25% on raised 2026 revenue guidance













Luke Juricic



14 October 20262 min read

































  - [MXCT \\
    -13.46%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/MXCT/ "MXCT")


Investing.com -- MaxCyte Inc (NASDAQ:MXCT) shares jumped 25% Wednesday after the cell-engineering company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance following strong third-quarter results.

The company reported preliminary third-quarter core business revenue of approximately $8.1 million, up 26% YoY from the third quarter of 2025 and exceeding the analyst estimate of $7.02 million. MaxCyte also recorded Strategic Platform License Program-related revenue of more than $1.0 million, including a $1.0 million milestone payment received during the quarter.

MaxCyte raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $34 million from prior guidance of $30 million to $32 million, surpassing the analyst estimate of $31.45 million. Core business revenue is now expected to reach approximately $28 million, compared to previous guidance of $25 million to $27 million. SPL Program-related revenue guidance increased to approximately $6 million from approximately $5 million, comprising roughly $4 million from milestone payments and approximately $2 million from commercial royalties.

The company attributed the third-quarter outperformance to accelerated instrument purchasing from a large customer, which was originally anticipated to occur in the fourth quarter. The updated guidance reflects approximately 15% YoY growth in core business revenue for the second half of 2026.

MaxCyte is currently supporting more late-stage clinical programs under its SPL partnerships than previously, including two pivotal trials with potential approval as early as next year. The company will report full third-quarter financial results, including royalty revenue, on November 10, 2026.

MaxCyte warned that preliminary third-quarter results are unaudited and subject to change pending completion of the company's quarterly closing process and review procedures.

Investing.com -- Consumer artificial intelligence agents could reshape online shopping, payments and financial services, but their success will depend on how established companies respond, according to Bernstein.

The rapid growth of Muse, which can compare products and quotes, call businesses, send emails, fill forms, manage inboxes, cancel subscriptions and negotiate for users, has fuelled speculation about an "iPhone moment" for consumer AI. OpenAI has launched Dots, while Google is expected to improve Spark.

Amazon blocked Muse within two weeks of launch, citing lack of prior notification, failure to identify itself, apparent collection of customer credentials and access to account pages and order histories. Others, including Shopify, Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Wayfair, Dick's Sporting Goods, Ulta Beauty, Fanatics, Expedia and Instacart, have partnered with Muse for shopping and checkout.

Payments use Stripe's Link, one-time virtual cards or Shop Pay; PayPal integration is announced but not live, while Meta plans a transaction fee.

Bernstein expects selective access rather than blanket blocking. Muse is developing API connectors with retailers, although it currently mainly browses websites, fills forms and prepares orders for user confirmation.

Meta received more than 1,500 developer applications in under a week, but OpenAI's Instant Checkout, despite partnerships with Walmart, Etsy, Instacart and more than one million Shopify merchants, illustrates the challenges.

Cloudflare says AI-agent requests on its network rose over 1,700% in a year, while human traffic in heavily crawled retail and financial-services categories fell as much as 40%. More verification, human checkpoints and differentiated access to catalogues, prices and accounts could follow.

Agents could gain traction by simplifying high-friction tasks such as insurance, medical and school forms, travel planning and coordinating tickets, reservations, transport and shared costs. U.S. travellers view 277 pages of travel content and spend about five hours researching trips in the 45 days before booking.

Silicon Valley agent Instinct says around 40% of users provide a credit card within three weeks and it handles about $1 billion in annualised transactions, roughly half in travel, though its affluent, tech-forward users may not represent the broader population. Business applications could prove more monetisable.

Bernstein sees payments as a potential winner - more online transactions, including smaller purchases, could benefit Visa, Mastercard and processors Stripe, Adyen and Checkout.

Story continues

PayPal wallets could offer trust, protection, savings, rewards and payment optimisation. Affirm and Klarna may benefit from dynamic underwriting, interest-bearing loans for near-prime and subprime borrowers, zero-interest prime loans and clearer terms.

# MAAS Group Says Firmus Contracts on Track After AI Infrastructure Firm Scraps ASX Listing













MT Newswires



9 October 20261 min read

































  - [MGH.AX \\
    +3.86%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/MGH.AX/ "MGH.AX")


![MT Newswires - Shutterstock](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/6eab2a46dc7d351aa99040acd39d261d43f31f1f1afd3f272c345113f1d8a321/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fmt_newswires_au_792%2Faa60b555ef15cae2b56eac352e00670d.png)

MT Newswires -Shutterstock

MAAS Group Holdings (ASX:MGH) said its unit JLE Group is continuing to deliver on its existing contracts with Firmus after the artificial intelligence infrastructure company withdrew its application to list on the Australian bourse.

Firmus decided that, given recent market swings and current conditions, its initial public offering would not reflect its long-term growth prospects, and it will now seek funding from private investors and consider other public and private options.

JLE is building modular Power Cubes and carrying out related electrical work for Firmus' current AI factory projects, and has received work orders from Firmus totaling about AU$1.1 billion across fiscal 2026 and 2027.

MAAS has received payments of AU$373 million against those orders under the terms of its service agreement with Firmus, and expects the work to be completed by the end of 2027.

MAAS bought about 1.1 million ordinary shares and about 1.1 million preference shares in Firmus within the current year at an average cost of about AU$188 per share, or AU$3.76 per share, adjusting for Firmus' proposed 50-for-1 share split.

The listing was called off even though Firmus' advisers, a group that included JPMorgan, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and Morgans Financial, said demand far exceeded the shares on offer, the Australian Financial Review reported, citing an email from Morgans Financial.

Firmus is working on plans to list on the Nasdaq instead, AFR said.

UniSuper Chief Investment Officer John Pearce told ABC that while Firmus has a "compelling" story, its valuation is priced for perfection, adding that "so much has to go right to justify the valuation."

# ChronoScale stock jumps on $1B revenue target from AI deals













Luke Juricic



1 October 20262 min read

































  - [CHRN \\
    -7.92%](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CHRN/ "CHRN")


Investing.com -- Chronoscale Corp (NASDAQ:CHRN) shares rose 3% in after-hours trading Thursday following the company's announcement of an expanded customer agreement and a new customer deal that are expected to drive its annualized revenue run rate to $1 billion by the third quarter of 2027.

The Menlo Park, California-based accelerated compute platform provider said it signed a contract extension with an existing AI infrastructure customer and secured an agreement with a new customer. Together with existing contracts and the current deployment schedule, these agreements provide for $1 billion in annualized run-rate revenue by the third quarter of calendar 2027.

ChronoScale noted that achievement and timing of the contracted revenue remain subject to risks including successful and timely deployment of planned infrastructure capacity, availability of power and equipment, and the company's ability to access capital on acceptable terms.

"With these agreements, together with our existing contracts and current deployment schedule, we now have agreements in place that provide for $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate during calendar 2027," said Cenly Chen, Chief Executive Officer of ChronoScale.

The company also completed the sale of its Ekso Bionics business unit, which it said will allow it to focus operations and capital allocation on its core accelerated compute and AI infrastructure business.

ChronoScale was formed through the strategic combination of Applied Digital's cloud business and EKSO Bionics Holdings, Inc. The company now operates as an independent public entity focused on scalable GPU-based infrastructure optimized for AI training, inference and high-performance computing.

The company's platform is designed to address growing enterprise and AI-native demand for dedicated computing environments capable of supporting demanding AI workloads.
